ph-katipunan.title: Flag of the Katipunan
desc:
- The flag of the Katipunan (Kataas-taasan, Kagalang-galangang Katipunan ng mga Anak ng Bayan) was a red field with a white sun — the banner of the revolutionary society that launched the Philippine Revolution in 1896
- Founded by Andrés Bonifacio, the Katipunan used several flag variants
- The most common featured a white mythological sun (representing liberty) on a red field (representing the blood of revolution)
- **Construction:** a red field with a white sun device centred. Ratio approximately 2:3
trivia:
- The Katipunan was the revolutionary group that fought Philippine independence
- The flag represented the independence movement against Spanish rule
- Led the Philippine Revolution of 1896

ph-revolutionary.title: Flag of the First Philippine Republic
desc:
- The Philippine revolutionary flag designed by Emilio Aguinaldo featured a white triangle at the hoist with a golden sun and three stars, on a field of blue and red horizontal stripes
- First unfurled at the proclamation of Philippine independence on 12 June 1898, it is essentially the precursor to the modern Philippine flag
- The three stars represent Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao; the eight rays of the sun represent the first eight provinces that revolted
- **Construction:** a white equilateral triangle at the hoist, with a golden sun (eight rays) and three five-pointed stars
- Two horizontal stripes of blue (top) and red
- Ratio 1:2
trivia:
- The revolutionary Philippines flag represented the independence movement
- Preceded the modern flag and was used during the Spanish-American War
- Adopted when the Philippines declared independence from Spain
